messages:
julie-cs: FYI customer ACME corp on Dedicated (na-east) reporting mass 429s for generation endpoints and some 401s during retries. They say errors started ~09:12 UTC and billing shows skipped tokens for a subset of requests. Escalating.
ops-bot: [ALERT] region=na-east service=dedicated-inference severity=high cpu_util=92% alloc_fail_rate=12% autoscale_reason=quota_limit
sre-oncall: digging in. Do we have a tenant id or sample request/response from the customer?
julie-cs: tenant: acme-5421. Customer pasted one failing response:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "allocation_error",
  "message": "no available GPUs in pool: na-east-primary"
}
```

and an auth failure after retry:

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{ "error": "token_refresh_failed", "detail": "billing lock: account_pending_payment" }
```

They say retries triggered the billing check and then some tokens were not counted.

sre-oncall: odd — allocation failures shouldn't cause 401. Could be side-effect where token refresh webhook times out due to overloaded control plane.
dan: I see increased placement rejects in na-east logs around 09:11-09:18. Autoscaler did a scale-up but new instances failed accept because we hit GPU inventory quota in that AZ.
prashant: autoscaler logs:

```
scale_up_requested: 8 gpus
quota_check: false
reason: allocation blocked - regional_capacity_exhausted
```

maria: customer says noisy-tenant x-tenant-789 was spinning up many small low-priority jobs earlier which could explain fragmentation.
sre-oncall: can we repro in staging with the same flow? Need a short repro to validate fix and test fallback.
julie-cs: customer provided a repro sequence: 1) send 30 concurrent generation requests (model=tiny-emoji) 2) rapid retries on 429 with backoff 50-200ms 3) token refresh call for long-running sessions

prashant: trying to repro against staging-stress now. Initial note: our prefix cache is being hammered; continuous batching increases queue depth -> triggers placement rejects when fragment counts > threshold.

sre-oncall: immediate mitigation options:
- patch routing to divert new Dedicated allocs to na-west for acme-5421 only
- temporarily throttle tenant x-tenant-789 (noisy neighbor) via tenant QoS
- manually increase regional quota (ops approval) or open emergency pool from reserved-capacity

dan: I started a manual reroute for acme-5421 to eu-west1 (canary) — traffic transfer at 09:35 UTC. Watch latency & token accounting.

ops-bot: reroute job queued -> started. Migration id=mr-2648. Note: eu-west has ~60s cold start for some models.

maria: customer confirms partial success after reroute, generation errors dropped but some sessions show missing token counts in billing UI.

julie-cs: onboarding asked for a temporary billing hold while we investigate — can billing team pause ingestion for acme-5421?
sre-oncall: tagging billing. In parallel, we need to confirm the control plane timeout that caused 401s. Hypothesis: placement backlog -> token refresh webhook timed out -> refresh returned 401, client abandoned and retried -> additional allocation pressure.

prashant: I have log snippet showing webhook 504s during heavy placement load. Suggest increasing webhook timeout to 15s for control plane or queuing refresh requests.

maria: also found noisy tenant pattern: 100s of tiny sessions with TTL=30s causing fragmentation. We should apply soft quota on concurrent sessions per tenant while we do deeper cleanup.

sre-oncall: action list:
1) prashant to open infra PR to add short-term increase to webhook timeout and enqueue refreshes (owner: prashant) — ETA 2h
2) dan to monitor reroute and confirm token accounting in eu-west (owner: dan) — ETA 30m
3) ops to provision emergency reserved GPUs for na-east if available (owner: sre-oncall) — ETA 1h
4) julie-cs to coordinate with billing for temporary hold (owner: julie-cs) — ETA 15m
5) maria to apply tenant throttle to x-tenant-789 (owner: maria) — ETA 10m

julie-cs: customer priority P1. They asked for status updates every 20 minutes.

dan: reroute metrics: in-flight requests dropped by 70% in na-east after diversion. eu-west latency up ~120ms for acme but within SLO.

ops-bot: reserved-pool request submitted -> pending approval from capacity-committee.

prashant: PR opened: infra/webhook-timeout-hotfix (link: https://git.redwood/infr/PR/549) — staging tests pass. Requesting hotfix deploy to canary control-plane.

sre-oncall: approving hotfix deploy to canary now. Will monitor for 401 recurrence.

julie-cs: billing responded: placed temporary ingestion hold for acme-5421. They will not be charged for any missing tokens while we investigate.

maria: applied tenant throttle to x-tenant-789: concurrent_sessions cap=40. Early reduction in fragment churn observed.

sre-oncall: 10:15 UTC update: after reroute + throttle + webhook timeout patch in canary, no more 401s reported. Placement rejects decreased to <1%.

julie-cs: customer acknowledges service restored for now, still watching. They requested a postmortem and concrete plan to prevent repeat.

sre-oncall: next steps: full rollout of webhook patch, revisit autoscaler quota logic (avoid scale_up requests when regional inventory tight), add tenant QoS detection for fragmentation, and improve billing token reconciliation during reroutes. Assigning follow-ups in JIRA.

julie-cs: thanks team. I'll keep customer updated and schedule a postmortem with SRE + Billing + Product. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: closing incident thread for active mitigation. Will reopen if any regression.
